label: early original-phase step right after m/i/d, strongest in o-initial sequences (sparse conjunction)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps) that fires only in the original phase at t=2..9 (peak t=3-4) and at the <DEL> step, never in the copy phase. Activation is strongly enriched when the previous input is m (18x lift, ~52% of mass) or i/d, when m/d/i appear two steps back, and when the first token is o (12x); top examples are prefixes like o d m / o m m / o i m followed by 3, g, y. It looks like a conjunction over the hidden-state contents of the first few tokens, not any simple per-step rule: prev_tok==m alone has 52% recall at 1% precision, and adding first_tok==o raises precision only to ~7%. The best simple predicate reaches dev F1 ~0.11. Firing magnitude is highest for o-initial prefixes containing m; I did not find any other magnitude driver.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=m (+6.32), orig0=o (+5.61), prev_tok=i (+5.05), prev2_tok=m (+4.41), prev_tok=r (+3.79), prev2_tok=i (+3.68). Lower it: phase=2 (-5.70), prev3_tok=q (-3.11), orig0=s (-1.91), out_tok=- (-1.15).
